steps.title: Read the table
steps.body: Type `enable`, then `show ip bgp`. Look at 198.51.100.0/24: two paths, one marked `>`. Hand in its next hop with `submit BEST=...`, and the reason it won with `submit REASON=as-path` style (weight, local-pref, as-path or med).

steps.title: Prefer Moonbase
steps.body: In `conf t`: `route-map MOON-FIRST permit 10`, then `set local-preference 200`, then `exit`. Apply it: `router bgp 65010`, `neighbor 198.18.0.1 route-map MOON-FIRST in`. Then `end`, `clear ip bgp * soft` and `show ip bgp`: the `>` moves to 198.18.0.1 with LocPrf 200.

objectives.label: Moonbase is now the best path

steps.title: Refuse the hijack
steps.body: Find the bad route in `show ip bgp` and name the AS that originated it: `submit HIJACK=<AS number>` (the last number in its path). Then in `conf t`: `ip prefix-list NO-GRID seq 5 deny 192.168.0.0/16 le 32`, `ip prefix-list NO-GRID seq 10 permit 0.0.0.0/0 le 32`, and in `router bgp 65010`: `neighbor 203.0.113.1 prefix-list NO-GRID in`. `end`, `clear ip bgp * soft`, `show ip bgp`.

objectives.label: Prefix list NO-GRID denies the Grid's own space and permits the rest
NO-GRID applied inbound on Earth's session
The hijacked route is gone from the table

steps.title: Read a community
steps.body: Run `show ip bgp 10.99.0.0`. Moonbase tagged that route. May Skyport pass it on to Earth Relay, another AS? `submit EXPORT=yes` or `submit EXPORT=no`.
